newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ROBSON AND SOUNESS FINED BY F.A..
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON AND SOUNESS FINED BY F.A..

text.p: The English Football Association said on Monday they had fined Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson and Southampton boss Graeme Souness for misconduct.
The fines follow a plea by premier league referees for managers to observe a 30-minute "cooling off" period before confronting officials at the end of matches.

Robson was fined 1,500 pounds ($2,367), severely censured and warned about his future conduct over remarks made to referee Michael Riley after the match with Nottingham Forest at the City Ground on August 24.
Souness was fined 750 pounds ($1,184) and warned after remarks made to Riley after the Leicester-Southampton clash at Filbert Street on August 21.
F.A. spokesman Steve Double said: "This is a good time to point out that we are asking managers to observe a 30-minute cooling period after the final whistle before approaching match officials.

"It is at the discretion of the referees as to what extent they want to discuss things but hopefully the 30-minute period will put an end to the heat-of-the-moment remarks which we have been experiencing in recent times.
